Gautam Gambhir

Gautam Gambhir was a left-handed opener who made a habit of being there when India needed him most, and he has carried that habit into coaching.

Where it began

He was born in New Delhi on 14 October 1981 and picked up a bat at 10. He went to Modern School in the city and learned his cricket from Delhi coaches, Sanjay Bharadwaj among them. In 2000 he was among the first group of young players taken on by the National Cricket Academy in Bangalore. He played his first Test in 2004, against Australia.

The player

In 58 Tests he made 4,154 runs at 41.96, with nine hundreds and 22 fifties. His best was a double century against Australia in 2008, part of a golden spell in which he scored hundreds in five Tests running. Only Don Bradman has strung together more, and no other Indian has managed it.

In 2009 the ICC named him its Test Player of the Year, and for a while he was the top-ranked Test batter in the world. In New Zealand that year he batted for more than five sessions to save a Test, and India went on to win a series there for the first time in 41 years. In white-ball cricket he made 75 in the final of the World Twenty20 in 2007 and 97 in the final of the World Cup in 2011, and India won both.

What made him special

He was a fighter at the top of the order. He liked to bat for a long time, and he was at his best when the match was going the wrong way. With Virender Sehwag, his Delhi team-mate and good friend, he made one of the great Indian opening pairs: one attacked, the other stayed, and the scoreboard rarely stopped.

Like most openers he had leaner seasons, and in one-day cricket he had a knack for stopping in the nineties on big occasions. That 97 is the famous one, though India were too busy celebrating to mind. He bowled a little in Tests too, without ever troubling the wicket column.

Away from the middle

He led Kolkata Knight Riders to the IPL title in 2012 and again in 2014, then came back as their mentor and helped them to a third in 2024. Sehwag once named him the Second Wall, after Rahul Dravid. He received the Arjuna Award in 2008 and the Padma Shri in 2019, and served a term in the Lok Sabha for East Delhi between 2019 and 2024. His foundation runs community kitchens in Delhi and plants trees to help clean the city's air.

In July 2024 he became head coach of India. Under him they have won the Champions Trophy and the Asia Cup in 2025 and the T20 World Cup in 2026.

And finally

He finished his playing days in December 2018 with a hundred for Delhi in his last innings, his 43rd in first-class cricket. Some people leave a party quietly. He made sure the last song was a good one.
